title: fix(plugin-detail): format every record-page timestamp in the display locale
body:
Part of #9786.

## Why `Part of` and not `Fixes`

The nine files the card names are repaired and an instrument is left behind, but two things survive this branch and both are the card's own: the class exists outside `packages/plugin-detail` (measured below, report-only, and outside this card's fence), and the card's central question — whether a repo-wide gate should exist — is still open. Closing the card on this merge would close it over both.

## FIRST — the census, re-derived on the current tip

Read on `4b5772299` (the branch point, `origin/main` at the time), UTC 2026-09-18T13:56Z, with comments masked by the repo's own `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`:

```
CODE  ActivityTimeline.tsx:67: return date.toLocaleDateString();
CODE  ConcurrentUpdateDialog.tsx:82: return d.toLocaleString();
CODE  DiffView.tsx:49: return [new Date(value).toLocaleString()];
CODE  HistoryTimeline.tsx:86: return d.toLocaleString();
PROSE PointInTimeRestore.tsx:49: * have a fourth `d ago` branch and fall through to `toLocaleDateString()`,
PROSE PointInTimeRestore.tsx:50: * while this one stops at hours and falls through to `toLocaleString()` —
CODE  PointInTimeRestore.tsx:67: return date.toLocaleString();
CODE  RecordActivityTimeline.tsx:157: return date.toLocaleDateString();
CODE  RecordComments.tsx:56: return date.toLocaleDateString();
CODE  RecordMetaFooter.tsx:91: return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, {
CODE  ThreadedReplies.tsx:43: return date.toLocaleDateString();
--- CARD INSTRUMENT on origin/main: CODE 9 + PROSE 2 = TOTAL 11
```

**The card's 11 is 9 call sites plus 2 lines of prose.** `PointInTimeRestore.tsx` is listed in the card's table with 3 sites; it has one. The other two are its doc comment explaining why its tail differs from its siblings'. The card's instrument had no way to tell code from prose, which is what printing lines rather than counts catches.

**The card's lit control no longer lights.** The card cites `DetailView.tsx`'s two `Intl.NumberFormat(undefined` sites as the probe's control. PR #9777 has landed since, and those two now read `displayLocale` — so a reviewer who re-ran the card's probe today would get a control of 0 and could not tell a broken query from a clean file. The control used here instead prints every `Intl.` / `toLocale` line in `DetailView.tsx` and reads it, which stays lit through the repair.

## SECOND — the floor: what the instrument cannot see, and how that was tested

The narrow probe was replaced by a superset with no argument-shape condition at all: every `Intl.` and every `toLocale` line in `packages/plugin-detail/src`, read one by one. That superset returned two lines the card's probe could not:

1. **`HistoryTimeline.tsx:108` — `new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(locale, …)`.** `locale` is the component's own optional prop, whose doc comment declared the defect in words: "Defaults to browser locale". No call site in this repo passed it, so at runtime it was `undefined` on every render. This is exactly the class the card said its count could not include, it was real, and it is site number ten.
2. **`InlineFieldInput.tsx:501` — `d.toLocaleDateString('en-CA')`.** Read for intent and deliberately **not** repaired: it builds the `value` of a native date input, which HTML defines as `YYYY-MM-DD`. It is an ISO formatter, not a display locale, and moving it onto the session locale would blank the picker for every tenant whose locale writes dates any other way. Declared as the one exemption in the census pin, with that reason, so a second hard-coded tag reddens instead of inheriting a blanket pass.

The structural answer to "a variable that is `undefined` at runtime" is not a better grep. The pin therefore patches `Intl.DateTimeFormat` / `NumberFormat` / `RelativeTimeFormat` / `ListFormat` / `PluralRules` / `Collator` and `Date.prototype.toLocale*` during each render and inspects the argument each call actually received. That sees through variables, defaults and spreads.

## THIRD — the instruments

**`detailTimestamps.displayLocale-9786.test.tsx`** — renders every surface twice, once under a declared `de-DE` tenant locale and once under `en`, with the UI language pinned to `en` on both legs so the only variable is the `Intl` tag, and requires the two readings to differ. Before this change both legs came from the machine and were byte-identical whatever the machine was, so this assertion is red on every runner including a German one. Literal `de-DE` and `en` faces are asserted alongside, and the runtime tripwire covers `RecordMetaFooter`, whose absolute face is a tooltip child Radix keeps out of the DOM until the tooltip opens.

**`machineLocaleCensus-9786.test.ts`** — reddens when a new bare, `undefined`-argument or hard-coded-tag call site appears anywhere in this package's source. It masks comments before counting (so it cannot repeat the card's prose over-count), carries width guards so a scan that silently narrows goes red instead of quiet, pins its own matcher against a fixture of all six shapes, and pins the declared exemption so deleting the `en-CA` call without deleting its entry is also red.

No new gate was added — the dispatch does not authorise one, and the repo-wide question stays with the card.

## Ablations — four, each with the mutation proved on disk by blob hash and the restore proved by hash equality plus an empty `git diff HEAD`

| mutation | what it proves | result |
|---|---|---|
| `RecordMetaFooter` back to `Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, …)` | a surface with no observable DOM face is still covered | **2 files red** — census offender list, and the tripwire row for that file |
| `ActivityTimeline` back to a bare `toLocaleDateString()` | the ordinary shape | **2 files red, 4 assertions** |
| `HistoryTimeline` back to the raw optional prop (still passes a variable) | the invisible class, and the division of labour | **behavioural pin red, census pin GREEN** — as designed: no source scan of any shape can see this one |
| all nine files reverted to the branch point at once | a blanket revert must not cost one assertion | **27 distinct assertions red across all nine files** |

**An assertion that stayed green where a naive reader expects red, reported rather than hidden:** the `keeps its en face under an en session` rows pass on the broken tree too, because this runner's machine locale resolves to the same face as `en`. That is precisely why the differential assertion, not the literal table, is the load-bearing one.

**A weakness the ablation found, and the pin was strengthened rather than shipped.** The first blanket ablation reddened the tripwire row for eight of nine files and left `ThreadedReplies` green: its reply list renders collapsed, so the component's own call never happened and the row was satisfied by locale-taking calls the surrounding i18next machinery makes. The row now opens the list and requires an observed call carrying the declared `de-DE` tag, which nothing but the surface under test passes. Re-ablated: nine of nine red.

## The sweep

Every test anywhere naming one of the nine changed files, with two controls in the same command (`useDisplayLocale`: 36 files, `zzNoSuchSymbolControl`: 0). Outside `packages/plugin-detail` the hits are prose mentions except `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx`, which reads `ConcurrentUpdateDialog.tsx` by path. Those trees were run.

A whole-tree grep for the strings this diff removes found **zero** transcriptions of the prop-doc sentence that changed, and no doc or test that pins any face this diff moves.

## Verify

| run | verdict |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — `Test Files 187 passed (187)`, `Tests 1811 passed (1811)` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/i18n/ + the app-shell / apps-console trees the sweep named` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — `Test Files 79 passed (79)`, `Tests 1428 passed (1428)` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run type-check` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run lint` | exit 0 — 0 errors, warnings all pre-existing |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` / `check:control-bytes` / `check:i18n-keys` / `check:i18n-drift` | exit 0 each |

The first `type-check` in this worktree was red with `Cannot find module '@object-ui/…'` throughout. That is an absent sibling build in a fresh worktree, not this diff: building the dependency closure turned it green with no source change.

## Pending changeset sweep

No pending changeset body is made false by this diff. The three nearest were read in full:

- `.changeset/9453-summary-chip-display-locale.md` (frontmatter: `'@object-ui/plugin-detail': patch`) — describes the chip, which this diff does not touch; its "every family in the chip's format switch is on one channel" stays true.
- `.changeset/7163-detail-timestamp-i18n.md` (frontmatter: `'@object-ui/plugin-detail': patch` and `'@object-ui/i18n': patch`) — describes the pack-key swap in the same helpers. This diff adds a parameter to those helpers and changes no key and no English value, so every sentence stands.
- `.changeset/9327-import-history-time-locale.md` (frontmatter: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`) — the same class in another package, untouched here.

## Out of scope, reported not swept

The same mechanical shape exists across many other packages in this tree. **None of those hits was read for intent**, and the one that was read shows why that matters: `packages/collaboration/src/CommentThread.tsx` uses a bare call as a deliberate `catch` fallback for a tag `Intl` itself rejected, which is not this defect. A raw scan over-reports. Pricing a sweep needs each hit read, and the gate question on the card needs answering first.
